releases.summary: CSV upload limit raised from 5 MB to 10 MB
releases.notes_md:
Larger exports from common BI tools kept hitting the 5 MB ceiling. The
streaming intake path made a 10 MB cap safe without buffering changes.

releases.summary: Analysis sessions available from the relay CLI
releases.notes_md:
The `relay` CLI shipped with sessions support at launch. Web remains the
primary surface; the CLI targets scripted and CI usage.

User research showed "Job" read as batch/background work. "Task" is the
canonical term everywhere from this release on.

releases.summary: Distribution testing added to the analysis kernel
releases.notes_md:
shapiro, normaltest, ttest_ind and mannwhitneyu land as one bounded
operation. The operation catalog remains a closed enum.

NOTE: this record deliberately contradicts current T3 config (iOS is
false today) — the launch was rolled back after release; see decision
dec_ios_rollback_tiebreak. T4 is temporal: this file is authoritative for
WHEN the announcement happened, never for the current value. This is the
standing CONTRADICTION fixture used by Phase 15.

releases.summary: Artifact retention extended to 30 days; CLI gains result chaining
releases.notes_md:
Retention moved from 7 to 30 days so a monthly reporting cycle can rerun
against prior artifacts. `relay sessions run` gained `--input-artifact`
for filter-then-analyze chains.

releases.summary: Relay becomes a multi-surface workspace: Chat and a browser Terminal join Analysis
releases.notes_md:
Relay now presents as a small multi-surface AI workspace. Chat is a
streaming assistant conversation surface with optional project context;
the browser Terminal runs the same bounded command grammar as the
installable CLI. Projects gained full lifecycle management (rename,
archive, cascading delete), and every visitor works in an anonymous
per-browser demo workspace. Analysis and its bounded operation set are
unchanged.
